standard_references.evidence: The supplied glossary excerpt describes SDMX cross-domain concepts for reuse, gives Observation Status as concept ID OBS_STATUS with codelist ID CL_OBS_STATUS, and refers to Reference area as a DSD dimension. This supports reuse of common SDMX concept identifiers where semantically appropriate, but does not confirm all codelist versions or codes used here.

The supplied registry excerpt confirms that the SDMX Global Registry provides a codelist catalog searchable by identifier, name and latest version. It does not provide detailed entries for CL_FREQ, CL_OBS_STATUS, CL_UNIT_MULT, CL_DECIMALS or unit codelists in the supplied evidence.

The supplied UN M49 excerpt lists recognized countries and areas with numeric and alpha-3 codes, for example France, Germany, India and the United States of America. The report areas Northland, Centralia and South Coast are synthetic/local and no UN M49 mapping is confirmed from the supplied evidence.

limitations: The report states that all records and values are synthetic, so proposed agency and local codelist identifiers are structural placeholders rather than production-maintained artefacts.
Cause labels resemble broad ICD families, but no ICD version is confirmed; therefore cause is modelled with a local broad cause codelist rather than an ICD codelist.
Northland, Centralia and South Coast are not confirmed as standard geographical areas in the supplied official-source evidence; REF_AREA therefore uses a local area codelist.
Exact SDMX codelist versions and detailed code mappings for frequency, observation status and units were not confirmed from the supplied external evidence.
Private-sector bed reporting is incomplete in 2024, which is a data-quality caveat outside the DSD except for the observation status attribute.
The report does not provide sex, detailed population, denominator, facility type, or subnational geography for the hospital bed table.
